properties.label: Route
properties.description: Directed origin–destination pair; aggregate key for network logistics.

properties.label: Hub airport
properties.description: Airport with high outbound connection volume (derived by analytics threshold).

properties.label: Time window
properties.description: Named local-time band for scheduling analytics (HHMM on airport clock).

properties.label: Morning peak
properties.description: Typical business travel band 06:00–09:59 local (crsDepTime 600–959).

properties.label: On-time flight
properties.description: FAA on-time: arrDelay <= 15 AND depDelay <= 15 AND not cancelled.

properties.label: Delayed flight
properties.description: arrDelay > 15 OR depDelay > 15 (FAA delay threshold, minutes).

properties.label: Minor delay
properties.description: 16–30 minutes past FAA on-time threshold.

properties.label: Moderate delay
properties.description: 31–60 minutes.

properties.label: Severe delay
properties.description: More than 60 minutes.

properties.label: Delay breakdown
properties.description: Attributed delay minutes per DOT cause on a single flight.

properties.label: On-time performance KPI
properties.description: Ratio of OnTimeFlight to completed Flight in a scope (carrier, route, window).

properties.label: Delay attribution share KPI
properties.description: Share of total delay minutes by DelayReason in a scope.

properties.label: primary delay reason
properties.description: Argmax of carrierDelay, weatherDelay, nasDelay, securityDelay, lateAircraftDelay (non-null).

properties.label: measuresKPI
properties.description: Links aggregated KPI instances to contributing flights (materialized in analytics layer).

properties.label: isHub
properties.description: True when airport exceeds hub traffic threshold in a reference period.

properties.label: scheduledInWindowClass
properties.description: TimeWindow class name from business rules (MorningPeak, EveningPeak, …).

properties.label: flightStatus
properties.description: OnTimeFlight, DelayedFlight, CancelledFlight, DivertedFlight.

properties.outcome: Boeing ist Marktführer (14,5 Mio. Segmente 2000–2008); branchenweiter OTP-Rückgang 2003→2007; 2007 schwächstes Jahr; operative OTP-Überprüfung für Boeing empfohlen.
properties.scenario: Welche Hersteller flogen 2000–2008 die meisten Segmente und welche OTP pro Jahr?
properties.reasoning:
1. Ontologie-Auflösung: Flight → assignedAircraft → Plane.manufacturer auf flights + planes.
2. Aggregation 2000–2008: Boeing führt mit 14,5 Mio. Segmenten (segmentRank=1 → marketLeader).
3. OTP-Klassifikation: FAA 15-min-Regel (OnTimeFlight) pro Jahr und Hersteller.
4. Trend 2003→2007: otpTrend(declining) bei allen Top-5 → punctualityRisk(elevated).
5. Schwachjahr 2007: weakOtp2007 für Airbus, Bombardier, McDonnell Douglas.
6. Boeing >40% Top-5-Anteil → fleetDominance(BOEING).
7. Marktführer + sinkende OTP → industryWideStress(2000-2008).
8. Empfehlung: recommendOTPReview(BOEING) — dominante Flotte, fallende Pünktlichkeit.
properties.content: Welche Hersteller flogen 2000–2008 die meisten Segmente und welche OTP pro Jahr?
